topic: Neural Network Learning: The Intuitive Guide to Backpropagation
target_audience: Introductory Data Science students or tech-savvy hobbyists

sections.title: The Big Picture: Learning via Trial and Error
lecture_lines: Neural networks learn by minimizing prediction errors.
Meet Robo-Chef, our robot learning to bake cakes.
It starts with guesses and adjusts through feedback.
animations: Fade in 'Robo-Chef' icon (#00FFFF) and a 'Cake' icon on screen.
Show a slider moving to '50 mins' (Guess) while '30 mins' (Target) is marked in #00FF00.
Flash background red (#330000) and shift the slider handle from '50' toward '30'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Anatomy of a Decision (Weights & Biases)
lecture_lines: Neurons use "knobs" called weights to process data.
Each knob determines an input's influence on results.
A bias sets the starting point for every decision.
animations: Display labels 'Temperature' (#FFD700) and 'Size' (#ADFF2F) with numerical inputs.
Show two dial icons labeled 'Weights' (#00BFFF) that rotate to show adjustment.
Show a 'Bias' slider (#FF69B4) moving horizontally to set the starting point.

sections.title: The Forward Pass: Making a Guess
lecture_lines: The forward pass is the network's first guess.
It takes cake temperature and size as inputs.
Weights multiply these inputs to calculate their importance.
Adding the bias produces a final time prediction.
Robo-Chef now has a guess for the baking time.
animations: Draw arrows pulsing from 'Inputs' to a central 'Neuron' circle (#FFFFFF).
Animate 'Weights' dials rotating as data 'passes' through them.
Pop up a box labeled 'Prediction: 20 min' (#FFFF00) at the end of the flow.

sections.title: The Loss Function: Measuring the 'Ouch'
lecture_lines: Loss measures the gap between prediction and reality.
A large gap means a high error or "ouch."
We visualize this loss as a deep valley.
animations: Draw a white parabolic curve (Loss Curve) across the center.
Place a red ball (#FF0000) on the high slope of the curve.
Show a vertical line between 'Guess' and 'Reality' labeled 'Loss' (#FF4500).

sections.title: Backpropagation: The Blame Game
lecture_lines: Backpropagation traces the error back to its source.
We calculate which knob contributed most to the mistake.
This "blame" is mathematically known as the gradient.
We move backward through the layers using the chain rule.
The robot finds exactly which settings were wrong.
animations: Show red error pulses (#FF0000) traveling backward from output to inputs.
The 'Weights' dials glow red and display 'Blame' percentages (80%, 20%).
Trace the path of the gradient backward through the network diagram.

sections.title: Gradient Descent: Turning the Knobs
lecture_lines: Gradient descent uses the blame to adjust the knobs.
We nudge weights in the opposite direction of error.
Imagine a ball rolling down toward the lowest loss.
A small learning rate ensures we don't overcorrect.
Each tiny adjustment brings us closer to perfection.
animations: Animate the red ball on the parabola rolling down toward the minimum.
Show the 'Weights' dials rotating slightly in the direction indicated by the 'Blame'.
Display a 'Learning Rate' label with a small green vector arrow (#00FF00).

sections.title: The Feedback Loop: Mastery through Repetition
lecture_lines: Learning requires repeating this cycle thousands of times.
Every cake baked makes the robot's guesses better.
Soon, Robo-Chef predicts the perfect time every time.
animations: Animate a circular 'Loop' arrow (#00FF00) spinning around the entire network.
Display an 'Epoch' counter rapidly incrementing from 1 to 1000.
Show a line graph where the 'Error' curve drops sharply and flattens near zero.
